title: operate a third-party managed desktop on AWS infrastructure
input: The VDI platform owner integrates its supported desktop management solution and assigned user pool.
action: WorkSpaces Core supplies supported desktop infrastructure for an integrated third-party VDI solution. The partner platform manages its configured brokering and desktop experience; responsibilities are split explicitly.
output: The employee connects through the integrated broker and uses the assigned desktop and corporate applications.
check: Verify partner compatibility, user assignment, connection recovery and infrastructure-versus-broker operational ownership.

title: isolate contractor access to an internal web application
input: The contractor authenticates through the configured identity provider and web-portal assignment.
action: Secure Browser hosts an isolated browser session with configured network access and session controls. The internal web application still authenticates the user and authorizes its business operations.
output: The contractor uses the approved internal web application without downloading unrestricted project data to the local endpoint.
check: Test session isolation, allowed sites, clipboard or file policy and removal of contractor access.

title: connect a managed endpoint to an assigned virtual workspace
input: The employee starts the registered thin-client device and its assigned virtual-desktop connection.
action: WorkSpaces Thin Client provides a managed endpoint for supported virtual workspace services. Device management configures the endpoint; the selected desktop service hosts the applications and data.
output: The employee works inside the remote desktop while local endpoint capabilities remain limited by the deployment policy.
check: Test device assignment, software updates, supported workspace connection and lost-device access removal.

service: Automated Forensics Orchestrator for Amazon EC2
title: preserve EC2 incident evidence before analysis
input: The responder identifies the suspected instance and approves the isolation and evidence collection scope.
action: The forensic orchestration solution coordinates configured evidence collection and isolation actions for the EC2 incident. Collection roles and runbooks must preserve source integrity and avoid unnecessary destructive changes.
output: The analyst examines protected disk or memory evidence in an isolated investigation environment.
check: Verify evidence hashes, chain of custody, collection completeness and controlled access before closing acquisition.

title: publish embedded sensor telemetry over a permitted connection
input: The embedded developer configures the board, sensor driver and supported secure networking components.
action: FreeRTOS schedules tasks on the microcontroller. The telemetry task reads the sensor and uses the configured networking or IoT libraries to authenticate and publish; the kernel itself is not a cloud messaging broker.
output: The receiving IoT application validates sensor payloads and stores accepted measurements.
check: Test task timing, reconnect behavior, secure credential handling and firmware update recovery on the actual device.

title: connect enterprise mobile equipment through a partner cellular solution
input: The enterprise owner selects a partner solution and defines subscriber, radio and application connectivity requirements.
action: Integrated Private Wireless combines partner cellular capabilities with the chosen AWS architecture. The partner radio and core components authenticate subscribers and carry allowed device traffic to enterprise endpoints.
output: The plant application accepts authorized equipment messages across the configured cellular and AWS connection.
check: Validate coverage, subscriber isolation, return routes and partner responsibility for radio and core recovery.

title: implement a reviewed feature from a development specification
input: The developer provides feature requirements, constraints and approved repository context.
action: Kiro assists the specification and implementation workflow with supported development capabilities. Generated plans and code changes remain proposed engineering artifacts; tests and review determine whether the feature is ready.
output: The developer inspects the implementation and submits the accepted diff through the repository's release process.
check: Compare behavior with acceptance requirements and reject unsupported dependencies or unintended access changes.

service: Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA)
title: run a containerized order API on a managed OpenShift cluster
input: The platform team selects the ROSA cluster architecture, namespaces and approved container image.
action: ROSA provides the selected managed OpenShift platform on AWS. OpenShift schedules the order pods and routes admitted application traffic; application code validates orders and accesses its restricted database.
output: The customer invokes the deployed order API through the configured route and receives the committed result.
check: Test namespace policy, image deployment, pod failure, application route health and database access denial.

title: implement an agent that calls an authorized inventory tool
input: The developer defines the model, inventory tool and allowed agent task in application code.
action: Strands supplies an agent-building SDK that coordinates model reasoning and registered tool calls inside the application runtime. The inventory tool validates permissions before returning stock; the SDK is not an independently hosted cloud service.
output: The application returns the retrieved stock answer and records the permitted tool execution for review.
check: Test tool denial, malicious tool content, looping limits and model failure before deploying the agent application.

title: move a supported vSphere workload to an approved VMware cloud target
input: The virtualization owner inventories VM state, networking, licensing and the currently supported commercial target.
action: VMware Cloud on AWS historically supplied a VMware SDDC on AWS infrastructure. Migration uses the supported VMware tools and target entitlement; current procurement and service availability must be checked before selecting this destination.
output: The target vSphere application runs with validated network paths and protected data dependencies.
check: Test VM compatibility, final data synchronization, DNS cutover and rollback before retiring source capacity.
